data.name: Trenton
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old English tréntan meaning 'to stretch, to turn'. The name Trenton has its origins in Old English and translates to 'town by the treent'. The name gained popularity during the Middle Ages due to the existence of various towns named Trent in England and the River Trent in Britain.

data.cultural_impact: Trenton is a name that evokes a sense of history and heritage, particularly for those with English or European ancestry. Trenton also highlights the significance of waterways in history, as the name was derived from the River Trent in England.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Trenton can be derived from its Old English roots. The word "treent" means 'turn' and 'stretch'. This can be interpreted as a reminder to turn to God in times of need and to stretch ourselves spiritually towards Him. The name Trenton may also serve as a reminder of the biblical phrase "a new direction" (Jeremiah 6:16), inspiring individuals to seek a renewed sense of purpose and spiritual growth.
